title: Hegseth’s dubious low-T screening may flag up to 25 percent of the Army
gist: A JAMA study of 479 male active-duty Army members estimates that about 26 percent would test below 300 ng/dL under Pentagon screening thresholds (15 percent at the CDC's 264 ng/dL), far above the at-most-1-percent prevalence of true male hypogonadism. The article argues the mandatory screening announced by Pete Hegseth will trigger many unnecessary follow-ups and overtreatment.
